raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies a recurring conversational routine, printed access, and optional messaging. Seven frequent attendees found the repeated structure helpful, supporting retention of that scaffold. The concrete limit is five occasional attendees struggling to enter conversations familiar to their partners; continuity may benefit some while hindering entry for others, but causation is unproved. Of 72 slips, 49 reported the speaking target and 48 named the intended preparation task. These do not establish success across 97 attendances; missing slips, untimed speech, and unlinked weeks limit inference. Coordination sometimes exceeded 90 minutes. Pair delays and partner changes identify friction without establishing its cause.

openings.claim: A self-contained opening prompt with alternating short speaking turns may help occasional attendees enter conversation while retaining the familiar session structure.
openings.delta: Make entry independent of shared prior-session context without requiring public proficiency labels or prior attendance.
openings.prediction: Compared with ordinary prompts, occasional attendees will start substantive speech sooner and report easier entry; frequent attendees will retain useful practice. If only formation delays matter, post-pairing entry measures should change little.
openings.probe: Within existing sessions, randomly offer pairs either the ordinary opening or a self-contained opening with alternating turns. Anonymously observe time from seating to each partner's first substantive contribution and speaking distribution; collect usefulness and optional attendance-frequency reports. Record added volunteer minutes.
assumptions: Opening prompts fit existing printing and session time.
Observed sessions are not sufficient alone to establish six-session success.

openings.claim: A visibly dated, single next-task box on every printed sheet may reduce confusion between current and earlier preparation instructions.
openings.delta: Distinguish instruction-version confusion from failure to obtain instructions.
openings.prediction: Among recipients, earlier-task answers should decrease; errors concentrated among nonrecipients would instead indicate an access problem.
openings.probe: Introduce the box using existing printing. On anonymous exit slips ask which dated sheet was received and the next task; compare error categories with baseline and log preparation-related coordination minutes.
assumptions: The intended next task is settled before printing.
Dating alone does not provide absent learners with advance access.
Before-after changes cannot establish causation alone.

raw.assessment: Two interaction hypotheses preserve free, inclusive conversational practice within the existing room and session. The observations establish difficulties, but neither their causes nor either mechanism's effectiveness. Six-session success still requires all three stipulated measures.

openings.claim: Combine self-contained conversational scenario cards with alternating speaker/listener roles. At the role-handoff interface, each new speaker selects a fresh prompt and optional printed supports; partners restart from the same explicit scenario instead of inheriting one participant's prior-session context.
openings.delta: Scenario cards alone may leave one partner dominating; alternating roles alone may distribute turns in a conversation an occasional attendee cannot enter. Their interaction could make allocated turns usable, while retaining a predictable structure and requiring no public proficiency labels.
openings.prediction: The combination increases reported useful minutes beyond either component alone, particularly for attendees reporting unfamiliarity with the scenario, without extending the session.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, rotate consenting pairs among cards alone, alternating roles alone, both, and usual practice. Observe speaking-time distribution anonymously and collect useful-minute reports. Record setup and weekly coordination time; count blank outcome answers separately.
assumptions: Reusable cards can be derived from existing sheets within the coordination budget.
Participants can choose supports without needing proficiency categorization.
Anonymous pair-level comparisons are feasible; attendance variation limits causal confidence.

openings.claim: Combine a printed, calendar-dated preparation card with a conversational teach-back in the final pair round. At the card-to-explanation interface, each partner locates the next session's date, explains its task aloud, and checks their interpretation against the same card.
openings.delta: Dates can identify the right task without ensuring comprehension; teach-back can reinforce an outdated task. Together they could reveal both selection and interpretation errors while providing speaking practice.
openings.prediction: The combination reduces both earlier-task answers and blanks more than either component alone, without increasing volunteer message-answering time.
openings.probe: Compare date-only, teach-back-only, combined, and usual handouts across session groups; independently ask each participant to identify the intended next task afterward. Log preparation, printing, and message-answering minutes. Give all groups corrected printed information before departure.
assumptions: Cards state self-contained tasks and remain available on return after absences.
A short conversational teach-back replaces existing closing time.
Peer checks need little volunteer intervention; this remains untested.

openings.claim: Self-contained prompts may remove inherited-context barriers; alternating roles may distribute speaking opportunities. Their combination, with fresh prompts and optional supports at handoff, may make turns useful while retaining the familiar routine.
openings.discriminator: Earlier substantive contributions after seating distinguish entry barriers from pair-formation delay; combined gains beyond either component distinguish interaction from turn allocation alone.
openings.fit: Free, attendance-independent, no public proficiency labels; conversational practice within 75 minutes and existing staffing.
openings.probe: Across six sessions rotate consenting pairs among ordinary practice, cards alone, roles alone, and both. Anonymously observe entry latency and speaking distribution; collect usefulness, unfamiliarity and optional attendance-frequency reports; log setup and coordination minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Attendance variation limits causal confidence; reusable cards, support choices and observation feasibility remain assumptions.

openings.claim: One dated next-task box may prevent version confusion; conversational teach-back may reveal interpretation errors. Combining them may avoid rehearsing an outdated task.
openings.discriminator: Earlier-task errors among recipients indicate version confusion; nonreceipt indicates access difficulty. Combined improvement beyond dates or teach-back alone supports their interaction.
openings.fit: Printed, self-contained tasks require no smartphone/account; cards available on return. Teach-back replaces closing time and remains conversational.
openings.probe: Compare date-only, teach-back-only, combined and usual handouts; independently ask received-sheet date and next task. Separate earlier-task answers and blanks; supply corrected printed information before departure. Log printing, preparation and message-answering minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Dates cannot give absent learners advance access; low-effort peer checking is untested. Before-after evidence alone cannot establish causation.

Merged with A2; preserves version-versus-access distinction.
Merged with Z2; preserves interpretation interaction and correction.

post_distill.decision: Retain familiar structure and probe both hypotheses. Synthetic observations establish no effectiveness: 72 slips cover 97 attendances, speech was untimed and weeks unlinked. Six-session success still requires 80% useful-speaking reports, 85% correct preparation identification and coordination below 90 minutes weekly.
